providers.title: Code providers
providers.description: Connect the GitHub App to one or more organizations, then pick in GitHub which repositories get scanned.
providers.github_tagline: GitHub App · reads the code and comments on pull requests
providers.key_note: The App's private key is encrypted on the server. Each scan mints a one-hour token that lives only in memory.
providers.forget_confirm: This removes the key and the connection from this server. The App still exists on GitHub: delete it there if you no longer need it.

pending.gitlab: With a read-only project token, so access is limited to the projects you choose.
pending.bitbucket: With a read-only repository access token.
pending.azure: Through Microsoft Entra ID, the method Microsoft supports since 2025.

row.not_installed: App created, not installed on any account yet

repositories.batch_running: A batch is already running: wait for it or cancel it.
repositories.batch_limit: Up to 100; for more, scan the whole organization.

branch.help: Every scan of this repository reads this branch: manual, batch and re-verification. Leave it empty to use {{branch}}, the default branch.
branch.help_unknown: Every scan of this repository reads this branch: manual, batch and re-verification. Leave it empty to use the default branch.
branch.invalid: That isn't a valid branch name. Use letters, digits and . _ / -, without spaces or "..".

search.label: Search for a repository
search.partial: Partial results: this account's repository list is still being read from GitHub.

github.pem_too_large: That file is too large to be a .pem key
github.pem_invalid: That file doesn't look like a GitHub App private key (.pem)

open.title: Open the new GitHub App form
open.body: Under your personal account or an organization you administer (enter its name):

name.title: Name and homepage
name.app_name: GitHub App name: anything you like, e.g. (it must be unique on GitHub; add your team's name if it's taken).
name.homepage: Homepage URL: any URL of yours, e.g.

hooks.title: No OAuth or webhooks
hooks.callback: Leave Callback URL empty and "Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation" unchecked.
hooks.setup: Setup URL (optional, brings you back here after installing): and check "Redirect on update".
hooks.webhook: Under Webhook, uncheck "Active": the panel polls pull requests itself, so it doesn't need to be reachable from the internet.

permissions.title: Permissions: only these four
permissions.outro: Nothing under Organization or Account permissions, and no events. The less access the App has, the less damage a leaked key can do.

install_scope.title: Where it can be installed
install_scope.body: Under "Where can this GitHub App be installed?" choose Any account if you'll connect several organizations. Then click Create GitHub App.

key.title: Copy the App ID and generate the private key
key.body: The App ID is at the top, under "About". Scroll down to Private keys and click "Generate a private key": a .pem file downloads.

form.title: 7 · Connect it here
form.description: The panel checks with GitHub that the key belongs to that App before saving anything.
form.admin_only: Only an administrator can connect the GitHub App.
form.env_missing: The server has GITHUB_APP_ID in its environment, but it's missing: {{missing}}.
form.key_note: The key is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) on the server; it never comes back to the browser or shows up in logs. Afterwards, delete the .pem from your downloads folder.

install.next_connected: You can add another organization and choose its repositories.
install.next_first: Install it on the organizations you need and choose their repositories.
install.step_install: Click Install on GitHub and choose Only select repositories, picking the ones you want to scan.
install.step_detect: Come back and click Find installations, then select the organizations you want to use in this workspace.
install.installed_on: Accounts where the App is installed
install.returned: GitHub installed the App on {{account}} ({{kind}} · {{scope}}). Connect it?
install.returned_unknown: That installation doesn't belong to the GitHub App configured here, or it was removed. Install it again or use “Find installations”.
install.returned_plain: GitHub installed the App on {{account}} ({{kind}} · {{scope}}). Connect it?

permission_warning.excess_one: The App requests {{count, number}} extra permission.
permission_warning.excess_other: The App requests {{count, number}} extra permissions.
permission_warning.excess_body: Review the GitHub App's permissions; installed repositories keep the scope you chose.
permission_warning.missing: Missing permissions: {{permissions}}. Without them, pull requests aren't reviewed.
permission_warning.missing_pending: Missing permissions: {{permissions}} (a permission update is waiting to be accepted on the installation). Without them, pull requests aren't reviewed.

create.title: Create the GitHub App automatically (recommended)
create.description: GitHub opens with everything filled in: the name, the four permissions and the return to this panel (no webhook). You confirm there and come back connected; the App and its key belong to your account.
create.name: App name
create.any_account: Several organizations: let the App be installed on any account (otherwise only on the one that owns it).
create.note: The private key goes from GitHub straight to this server, encrypted; it never passes through your browser.
create.manual: Prefer to create it by hand?
create.organization_help: Leave it empty to create the App on your personal account.
create.name_help: It must be unique on GitHub; if it's taken, GitHub lets you change it on its page.

registries.title: Container registries
registries.description: For scanning private images: in New scan, choose Container image. Public images need nothing. Always use a read-only token.
registries.empty: Add one to scan private images.
registries.stored_note: Encrypted on the server; it never comes back to the browser or shows up in logs. Saving again for the same registry replaces it.
registries.admin_only: Only an administrator can save registry credentials.
registries.help: What to enter for each registry

docker.token: read-only access token (in Account settings, under Personal access tokens)

ecr.token: output of aws ecr get-login-password (expires after 12 h)

gar.token: key for a service account with Artifact Registry Reader

registries.private_blocked: Registries on your internal network (private IPs) are blocked so nobody can use the panel to reach internal services. To allow them, start the server with PITANGUS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_REGISTRIES=1.

list.title: Domains & APIs
list.empty_text: Add one you control and verify it.
list.read_only: Only an admin adds, verifies or removes domains.
list.confirm_remove: Its saved headers, test users, scope and scheduled scan are deleted. Nothing was scanned or imported against it.
list.confirm_remove_runs_one: Its saved headers, test users, scope and scheduled scan are deleted. Its scan or import and its findings stay.
list.confirm_remove_runs_other: Its saved headers, test users, scope and scheduled scan are deleted. Its {{count, number}} scans and imports and their findings stay.
list.added: {{host}} added. Verify it to scan it.
list.empty_member: An admin adds and verifies them.
list.confirm_remove_surface: It leaves the list. Nothing was scanned or imported against it.
list.confirm_remove_surface_runs_one: It leaves the list. Its scan or import and its findings stay.
list.confirm_remove_surface_runs_other: It leaves the list. Its {{count, number}} scans and imports and their findings stay.

add.title: Add a domain or API
add.description: Next, you'll prove you control it.
add.unreachable: Doesn't respond over HTTPS yet. You can still add it.
add.context_placeholder: What it does, how users sign in, sensitive data it handles…

verify.title: Verify {{host}}
verify.dns_intro: Add this TXT record at your DNS provider.
verify.dns_covers: Covers subdomains too. If it fails, try again in a few minutes.
verify.file_intro: Publish this file on your site.
verify.meta_intro: Add this tag to the <head> of your home page.
verify.name: Name
verify.copy_failed: Couldn't copy. Select the value and copy it by hand.
verify.failed_dns: No TXT record found at {{name}} yet.
verify.failed_file: Couldn't find the token in the file at {{url}}.
verify.until: Valid until {{date}}; checked again every day.

page.scope_exact: Only {{host}} is covered. Verify by DNS to add subdomains.
page.access_text: Headers that get past the login, sent when a scan uses them.
page.findings_empty: No findings yet. Scan it or import results from another tool.
page.not_found: This domain doesn't exist or was removed.
page.technologies_none: None named by the last web scan.

schedule.title: Scheduled scan
schedule.pick_weekday: Choose at least one day of the week.
schedule.pick_month_day: Choose at least one day of the month.
schedule.none: Not scheduled. Scans run only when someone launches them.
schedule.once_a_day: That day already has a scan, so the first scheduled one runs on the next matching day.
schedule.paused: Paused: the verification expired. Verify again to resume.

access.none: Scheduled scans see public pages only. Add test users or headers to reach what's behind a login.
access.outside: Signs in on {{host}}, outside the saved scope
access.full: At most {{max}} test users per scan.
access.summary_both: Signs in as {{names}} and sends the saved headers

access.name: Header name
access.saved_note: Encrypted. Nobody can read it again.
access.confirm_remove: Scans stop sending it, and its value can't be recovered.
access.check_help: An HTTPS page on this domain that only loads when signed in. Scans request it with these headers before and after crawling; if it doesn't answer 2xx, the scan is incomplete and marks nothing fixed.

scope.empty: No related hosts yet. Search for them or add one by hand.
scope.empty_manual: No related hosts yet. Add one by hand.
scope.invalid: {{host}} isn't a host name. Use name.example.com.
scope.already_root: That's the domain itself: it's always analyzed.
scope.count: {{count, number}} of {{max}} hosts analyzed besides the domain.
scope.passive_note: Found in public sources (certificate logs, passive DNS); nothing is sent to these hosts until a scan includes them. New hosts start excluded.
scope.last_search_one: Searched {{date}}: {{count, number}} name found, {{kept}} with public addresses.
scope.last_search_other: Searched {{date}}: {{count, number}} names found, {{kept}} with public addresses.
scope.capped_one: {{count, number}} more wasn't listed: a domain keeps {{max}} hosts at most.
scope.capped_other: {{count, number}} more weren't listed: a domain keeps {{max}} hosts at most.
scope.exclude_all_text_one: {{count, number}} host stops being analyzed. Scans will reach the domain itself only, until you mark hosts again.
scope.exclude_all_text_other: {{count, number}} hosts stop being analyzed. Scans will reach the domain itself only, until you mark hosts again.

test_users.title: Test users
test_users.text: Reusable test accounts for this domain. Pick them when you start a scan instead of typing credentials again.
test_users.name: Name
test_users.keep_saved: Leave it blank to keep the saved one.
test_users.totp_hint: The base32 key shown when you set up the authenticator, often under “Can't scan the code?”.
test_users.advanced: Advanced: login and check URLs, scope, notes
test_users.login_url_hint: Where the scan starts signing in. Blank opens the home page of the host below and follows the login link it finds.
test_users.applies_to_hint: The host this account belongs to: the domain or one of its subdomains.
test_users.saved_note: Encrypted. The password and the key can't be read again, only replaced.
test_users.remove_text: Scans stop signing in with it, and its password can't be recovered.
test_users.limit: Up to {{max}} test users per domain.
test_users.check_url_hint: A page only a signed-in user sees, like /account. After signing in, the scan opens it as this user: a redirect to the login, 401 or 403 means the sign-in failed. Blank: ZAP's own check decides.

disconnect.title: Disconnect domain
disconnect.text: Removes {{host}} from Pitangus and deletes its configuration:
disconnect.users: Its test users, with their passwords and TOTP keys
disconnect.scope: Its related hosts and saved scope
disconnect.runs_one: Its scan or import stays, with its findings, triage and tickets: still in Analyses and Findings.
disconnect.runs_other: Its {{count, number}} scans and imports stay, with their findings, triage and tickets: still in Analyses and Findings.
disconnect.final: Nothing was scanned or imported against it. Deleted credentials can't be recovered.
disconnect.final_runs: If you add {{host}} again, its history links back. Deleted credentials can't be recovered.

images.unlinked_hint: No analyzed repository is linked: the labels don't name one, or they name a repository Pitangus hasn't analyzed. Link it by hand so it joins that repository's evidence.
images.load_failed: Couldn't load the images. Try again in a moment.
images.none: There are no images on the list yet.
images.title: Container images
images.none_for_repository_admin: Choose one above to link it.
images.unlinked: {{image}} is back to what its labels say.
images.added: {{name}} added to the list. It isn't scanned yet.
images.added_queued: {{name}} added to the list, and its scan is queued.
images.already_analyzed: {{name}} was already on the list: it has been scanned before.

add.title: Add an image
add.description: Put a container image on the list without scanning it. You can link it to the repository it's built from and scan it whenever you want.
add.reference_hint: Registry, name and tag or digest. Docker Hub images can go without the registry (nginx:1.27).
add.built_from_label: Repository the image is built from
add.built_from_hint: A link set here wins over the image's OCI labels.
add.scan_now_hint: Queues the scan right away. Leave it unchecked to scan later.
add.no_repositories: No repositories yet: connect GitHub in Integrations to link one.

images.confirm_remove: It was never scanned, so no findings are lost; you can add it again.

link_dialog.title: Link images to {{name}}
link_dialog.description: Choose the images built from this repository. A link set here wins over the image's OCI labels.
link_dialog.empty: No images yet. Add one by its reference to link it.
link_dialog.more: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}}: search to narrow it down.
